summary: Post-migration KV-cache credit applied to parent org instead of subaccount after Dedicated migration
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that kv-cache hit credits generated after their Dedicated migration (2026-03-07 03:00 UTC) were applied to the parent org account instead of the newly created subaccount. This resulted in a show-stopping billing variance for their subaccount (missing credits) and a transient over-credit on the parent invoice.

Impact:
- BrightByte reports ~18k credit units (kv-cache hits) missing from subaccount ledger between 2026-03-07 and 2026-03-09.
- Customer-facing invoices show negative adjustment on parent org and higher payable amount on subaccount.
- Affects automated reserve/burst allocation behavior for Dedicated capacity; they observed burst throttles after credits were not applied.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant: brightbyte-dedicated-1
- Migration completed: 2026-03-07 03:00 UTC (orchestration run id: orchestration-20260307-3421)
- Region: us-east-1

Steps to reproduce / observed timeline:
1) 2026-03-07 03:00 UTC: Customer migrated to Dedicated; subaccount brightbyte-prod-sub created, routing changed to dedicated queue.
2) 2026-03-07 04:15 UTC: Several batch jobs started heavy embed + chat workload using cached prefixes (observed kv-cache hit spikes in serving runtime).
3) 2026-03-07 to 2026-03-09: Metering pipeline emitted kv-cache credit postbacks marking credits for parent org id instead of brightbyte-prod-sub.
4) 2026-03-10: Customer noticed invoice variance and opened ticket.

Logs / evidence attached:
- postback logs snippet: postback-service/2026-03-07/kvcache_hits.log (included lines show org_id: 01-parent-xyz for entries that match subaccount request_ids)
- orchestration run: orchestration-20260307-3421 (link to run in console)
- billing ledger export (CSV) for parent and subaccount 2026-03-07..2026-03-09 (uploaded to support bundle)

Initial hypothesis:
- Attribution mapping used during the Dedicated migration window may have cached the legacy org mapping; postback service used the top-level org id because subaccount creation event hadn't fully propagated to the billing lookup cache.
- Alternative: a race in the usage-postback enrichment job that maps runtime tenant -> billing entity when receiving batch events during migration.
investigation_notes:
Investigation timeline:
- 2026-03-10 10:20 UTC: Support triage by Aisha. Collected support bundle and escalated to Billing & SRE.
- 2026-03-10 14:05 UTC: Billing analyst (Helena Ortiz) inspected ledger; confirmed 18,120 credit units applied to parent org on 2026-03-07 04:17 UTC.
- 2026-03-10 16:30 UTC: SRE (Ravi Menon) pulled postback-service logs and found enrichment job logs showing 'tenant_lookup: cache_miss -> fallback_parent' around 04:16-04:19 UTC.
- 2026-03-11 09:00 UTC: Replayed a subset of postbacks from raw events to the staging billing-enrichment service with the updated subaccount mappings; replay assigned credits correctly to the subaccount.

Findings:
- A short-lived propagation delay (~2–4 minutes) between org/subaccount creation event (sent by orchestration) and the billing-enrichment service cache population allowed initial postbacks to default to the parent org.
- There is no evidence of duplicate credit creation; credits exist only on parent ledger.
- The orchestration run and postback timestamps align with the window.

Temporary workaround tried:
- Replayed affected postbacks into billing pipeline for the customer (staging first) and validated attribution.
- Billing team prepared a manual ledger adjustment script to move credits from parent -> subaccount pending automated fix.

Open questions / risks:
- How many other tenants migrated in same window were impacted? (possible broader blast radius)
- Does the same race impact other event types (reserve allocations, burst credits)?

Next steps (proposed):
1) Execute controlled replay for BrightByte's affected window in production after review (Billing + SRE).
2) Run a search for other recent dedicated migrations in 2026-03-07 .. 2026-03-08 and sample their ledgers.
3) Implement gating in postback-enrichment: if tenant mapping cache miss occurs and orchestration timestamp < 10 minutes, queue the postback for retry instead of applying to fallback parent.
4) Add end-to-end test to migration runbook to validate billing mapping propagation.

Estimated ETA for fix: 2026-03-15 for automated mitigation; manual replay and ledger adjustments targeted by 2026-03-12.
resolution: Work in progress. Billing has prepared a manual ledger adjustment that will be applied after a cross-check with customer. Planned manual adjustment scheduled for 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC (pending customer confirmation). Long-term mitigation design agreed (cache-miss gating + retry) and backlog ticket created in infra (INT-88901) for implementation.
resolution_notes:
Preliminary manual fix: move 18,120 kv-cache-credit units from parent org id 01-parent-xyz to subaccount brightbyte-prod-sub. Billing will issue a correcting invoice/credit memo for parent org and reissue credits on subaccount ledger. Customer must confirm acceptance of manual adjustment before finalizing.

Follow-ups assigned:
- INT-88901: postback-enrichment gating and retry
- INT-88902: migration runbook billing-propagation test

Customer communication plan:
- 2026-03-10: Aisha acknowledged ticket and requested logs.
- 2026-03-11: Marco provided investigation summary and proposed manual adjustment.
- 2026-03-12: Awaiting BrightByte confirmation to proceed with manual ledger adjustment.
